items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-09-30
items.q: Have you ever heard of Eloise Blackenstein? ... No heard of Eloise Blackenstein. That was a big time woman, Eloise Blackenstein. She was a big time. Sporting house she had.

ctx.x: No. Or would he play one house?

He played the first one house and another. Lot of houses. This house, that house. Hattie Rogers. You ever heard of that name Hattie Rogers? On Gravity Street. Hattie Rogers. Have you ever heard of Eloise Blackenstein?

items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-09-30
items.q: Elvish Blackenstein. She had a very popular girl in there with her, prominent.

ctx.x: You're where Larry and Katz is now in that neighborhood.

Yeah. Yeah, Pat King. She was almost as big as a little white. Elvish Blackenstein. She had a very popular girl in there with her, prominent. One of the most beautiful colored girls that would live in the world was in her house at that time. You might have heard talk of her. And it was Louise Aberdey. The most beautiful colored woman that ever lived on earth, I thought. Ever lived on earth. She was the most beautiful colored woman that God ever died on the cross for, I thought. And it was Louise Aberdey, her name…
